# Release Notes

## Major Features

### World Model Editor
A comprehensive world building system has been introduced, allowing for sophisticated indoor and outdoor structure creation:
- **Portal System**: Create seamless indoor/outdoor transitions with intelligent visibility culling for improved performance
- **Hierarchical Organization**: Organize complex structures with drag-and-drop mesh support and automatic bounding calculations
- **Advanced Lighting**: Full support for point and spot lights with real-time preview
- **Multi-Selection Tools**: Enhanced selection accuracy with search and filtering capabilities
- **Mesh References**: Support for both mesh components and nested world model instances

### Terrain System Overhaul
- **Level of Detail (LOD)**: Dynamic terrain LOD with smooth transitions reduces performance impact at distance
- **Terrain Holes**: Paint holes in terrain for caves, dungeons, and custom structures
- **Inner Vertex System**: Enhanced terrain editing precision with improved deformation and flattening tools
- **Improved Collision**: More accurate collision detection with proper edge handling

### Foliage System
Bring your world to life with dynamic vegetation:
- **GPU Instanced Rendering**: Efficient rendering of thousands of grass and plant instances
- **Multiple Layers**: Support for different vegetation types with individual density controls
- **Dynamic Shadows**: Foliage properly casts and receives shadows
- **Performance Controls**: Console variables for density and enable/disable settings

### Particle System
Create stunning visual effects with the new particle system:
- **Visual Editor**: Intuitive particle editor for designing effects
- **Spell Integration**: Particle effects can be attached to spells and abilities
- **Color Tinting**: Dynamic color modification for spell visual variations
- **3D Audio Support**: Positional audio for enhanced immersion

### Area Triggers
- **Interactive Zones**: Create teleport triggers, quest zones, and event areas
- **Visual Editor**: Drag-and-drop trigger placement with viewport support
- **Action System**: Configure multiple actions per trigger (teleports, spawn events, etc.)
- **Filtering Tools**: Easily manage and locate triggers on large maps

## Gameplay Systems

### Complete Inventory Refactoring
The inventory system has been rebuilt from the ground up:
- **Command Pattern**: Robust, testable inventory operations
- **Bag Management**: Proper handling of containers and nested bags
- **Equipment Validation**: Smart validation for proficiencies and item requirements
- **Database Persistence**: Reliable inventory saving and loading
- **Distributed Architecture**: Improved communication between World and Realm servers

### Talent System
- **Talent Trees**: Full talent system with multiple trees per class
- **Database Persistence**: Talents are saved and restored between sessions
- **Reset Functionality**: Players can reset their talents
- **Talent Points**: Automatic point allocation on level up
- **Drag & Drop UI**: Intuitive talent point allocation interface

### Friend System
- **Friend Management**: Add and remove friends with real-time notifications
- **Online/Offline Status**: See when friends come online or go offline
- **Friend Lists**: View all friends with their current status
- **Database Integration**: Friends persist across sessions

### Quest System Improvements
- **Item Credit Handling**: Proper quest item credit tracking
- **World Object Interaction**: Quest-specific world object usability
- **Quest Notifications**: Accept and abandon quest notifications

### Proficiency System
- **Data-Driven Design**: Item classes, subclasses, and proficiencies now configurable via data
- **Weapon Proficiencies**: Proper checking for weapon type requirements
- **Armor Proficiencies**: Validation for armor class restrictions
- **Editor Integration**: Manage proficiencies directly in the item editor

## Combat & Spells

### Creature AI Enhancements
- **Combat Behavior System**: Sophisticated AI combat decision-making
- **Stat-Based System**: Creatures now use a proper stat system like players
- **Threat Management**: Improved threat multiplier handling
- **Movement Prediction**: Creatures predict player movement for better positioning
- **Melee Range Fixes**: Creatures properly maintain attack range

### Spell System Improvements
- **Spell Visualization**: Data-driven spell visual effects system
- **Animation System**: Extensible animation notify system with timeline editor
- **Footstep Sounds**: Character footsteps play appropriate sounds based on surface
- **Cooldown System**: Client-side cooldown tracking with UI support
- **Aura Cancellation**: Players can cancel their own buffs
- **Reagent Checking**: Proper validation of spell reagent requirements

### Projectile System
- **Data-Driven Projectiles**: Configure projectile behavior and visuals in data
- **Spell Integration**: Attach projectiles to spells for ranged attacks

## Graphics & Audio

### Audio System Overhaul
- **FMOD Integration**: Professional audio engine with 3D positional audio
- **Sound Channel Management**: Priority-based channel allocation
- **Distance Attenuation**: Realistic sound falloff over distance
- **Per-Channel Controls**: Individual pitch and volume control

### Rendering Improvements
- **Deferred Renderer**: Modern deferred rendering pipeline integrated into editor
- **GPU Instancing**: Efficient rendering of repeated objects
- **Cascaded Shadow Maps (CSM)**: High-quality dynamic shadows
- **Fog System**: Atmospheric fog with UI controls and adjustable range
- **Material Improvements**: Better material queue sorting and alpha blending

### UI Enhancements
- **Hyperlink Support**: Clickable links in chat with color customization
- **Minimap System**: Functional minimap with party member icons and proper coordinate mapping
- **Loading Screen**: Professional loading screen during world transfers
- **Windows 11 Support**: Mica effects, dark mode, and rounded corners

## Editor Improvements

### World Editor
- **Viewport Panel Refactoring**: Cleaner, more organized interface
- **Transform Tools**: Inline transform mode buttons for quick access
- **Grid Snapping**: Configurable grid snap settings
- **Selection Raycaster**: Triangle-level precision for object selection
- **World Settings Panel**: Centralized terrain and UI settings

### Data Editors
- **Spell Effect Selector**: Searchable, categorized effect selection
- **Item/Spell Editor Refactoring**: Improved readability and consistency
- **Map Editor**: Better validation and spawn management
- **Quest Editor**: Enhanced UI with sectioning and helpful tooltips
- **Asset Management**: Delete folders and assets with confirmation dialogs

### Quality of Life
- **Entry Selection by ID**: Quickly jump to specific data entries
- **Asset Preview**: Preview meshes and other assets before use
- **Undo/Redo Support**: Better editor history management
- **Drag & Drop**: Consistent drag-and-drop across all editor windows

## Technical Improvements

### Performance Optimizations
- **Terrain LOD Caching**: LRU cache for terrain level-of-detail data
- **Iterator Debug**: Disabled in debug builds for faster iteration
- **Shader Optimization**: Full optimization even in debug builds
- **Input Layout Reuse**: Reduced DirectX overhead in D3D11 renderer
- **Entity Animation**: Optimized update code for better performance

### Infrastructure
- **Docker Support**: Containerized deployment for all server types
- **Database Migrations**: Proper schema migration support
- **Bruno API Collection**: API testing and documentation
- **Movement System**: More robust character movement with better collision handling
- **World Transfer**: Seamless attribute, inventory, and talent synchronization

### Code Quality
- **Test Coverage**: Extensive unit tests for inventory, equipment, and validation systems
- **Refactoring**: Improved modularity and maintainability across the codebase
- **Documentation**: Enhanced Doxygen comments and usage examples
- **Error Handling**: Better error handling for entity creation and asset loading

## Bug Fixes

- Fixed fullscreen mode causing window freeze on exit
- Fixed terrain tile rendering for empty tiles
- Fixed creature AI getting stuck out of attack range
- Fixed death/kill procs not triggering correctly
- Fixed wrong icon on cursor when dragging items/spells
- Fixed FMOD audio crash due to uninitialized channel index
- Fixed memory corruption in minimap rendering
- Fixed world not loading objects after map change
- Fixed realm name error responses in API
- Fixed aura effect handling for ModStatPct
- Fixed server crash on death by periodic auras
- Fixed character name blocking after character deletion
- Fixed bag removal when bags are not empty
- Fixed collision detection edge cases for walkable surfaces
- Fixed movement validation and position synchronization issues

---

**Note**: This release represents a significant evolution of the MMO platform with major systems for world building, gameplay mechanics, and visual quality. Many features are now data-driven, allowing for easier content creation and modification without code changes.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Kyoril/mmo/compare/build-32...build-35

### Editable Terrain

* Terrain can now be deformed and painted in the Editor
* Terrain Resolution has been increased to offer more details

### Improved spawn placement

* Units can now be spawned in the editor by simöly dragging and dropping them into the world
* Unit spawns are now visible in the world editor while in unit spawn mode
* Unit spawns can be moved around and edited directly in the world editor

### Pathfinding

* Pathfinding is now in the game. Creatures and Players can use it for movement calculations.
* A new Tool has been created: nav_builder
  * This tool builds nav meshes to be used by the server for one world and utilizes multi threading to make this process effective
  * In a later release, this tool might be merged into the world editor

### New Spell effects and gameplay features

* New spell effect: Charge. Makes the caster charge towards a target unit using pathfinding.
* New aura effect: ProcTriggerSpell. Allows proccing a spell under certain conditions such as performing a melee attack on a target
* New spell effect: Teleport. Supports teleporting a unit to a given location.

### Party System added

* Players can now invite other players to a party by typing /inv Playername
* A party has a limit of 5 members
* Party ui has been added
* A party leader can invit or kick members
* Parties are saved when logging of or server restarts
* Players see party member health and resource bars even when far away
* Players can target party members even when far away
* A new chat mode has been added: Party Chat. Type /p to use it when in a party. Only party members will see this chat, even across different worlds.

### New admin commands

* worldport <mapid> [x] [y] [z]
  Teleports your character to the given world and or location. If no coordinates are given, your current coordinates are used.
* port <playername>
  Teleports your character to the location of the given character. Works even if the target player is offline.
* summon <playername>
  Summons the given player to your location. Works even if the target player is offline.
* speed <meter per second>
  Changes the base movement speed of your Character to ghe given value in meters per second. Lasts until your character leaves the current world.

### Increased melee combat experience

* While battling, npcs will now face their attack target
* Added new feedback for missing hits as well as parried, dodged or blocked hits
* Fixed the display position of combat texts vertically

### Added sounds and music to the game

* The game can now play music and sounds
* Some Background Music was added to the Game in the title screen and in the world
* Ambience added to the world
* Added some sound effects like when opening the spell book

### Performance optimizations

* Added SIMD to some crucial math operations
* improved Bounding Box transform math
* Reduced D3D11 state changes
* Introduced octree to the scene manager fot increased performance while determining what to render and what not

releases.name: Space Showdown 2.0 — Wii Arcade Edition
releases.body:
Native Wii homebrew build of Space Showdown, a Megamania × Galaga style arcade shooter.

**Install:** unzip to the root of your SD card (it contains `apps/spaceshowdown/`), then launch from the Homebrew Channel. Or send directly: `wiiload apps/spaceshowdown/boot.dol`.

**Controls (sideways Wiimote):** D-pad moves · 2 fires · 1 bombs · + pause · − back · HOME quit. Classic Controller and GameCube pads also supported.

**Features:** formation dives, streaming squadrons, challenge stages, 4 bosses, tractor beams + dual fighter, chain multipliers, sharpshooter streaks, power-ups, 14 medals, daily challenge, top-10 high scores saved to SD.

Built from source with devkitPPC + SDL2-wii; all assets are generated procedurally from the Python source by `wii/game/tools/export_assets.py`. Tested on real Wii hardware (and Dolphin).

releases.name: v1.6.1-4 — webOS TV + Wii
releases.body:
One webOS TV fix, found and verified on real hardware.

## Fixed

**The app died at startup on some TVs, without printing a single line.** LG's
system SDL2 routes logging through PmLog, and that path calls a function pointer
that only gets filled in during `SDL_Init` -- with no NULL check. The game logged
while resolving its save directory and loading settings, all of that ahead of
`SDL_Init`, so the very first log line jumped to address 0 and killed the
process. There was no output because the thing producing the output was what
crashed.

Logging now prints the line itself when SDL is not yet up, in the same format
the normal output path produces, and startup brings SDL up before it does any
logging work. TVs that were already launching are unaffected -- this only
removes a crash on the ones that were not.

Wii and desktop builds are unchanged.

## Docs

The README's native refresh rate bullet now says desktop and web only. The webOS
UI layer does not appear to draw past 60 Hz, so the interpolated frames buy
nothing on a TV, and the bullet read as a promise of high-refresh play
everywhere.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mariotaku/FruitNinja/compare/v1.6.1-3...v1.6.1-4

releases.name: v1.6.1-3 — webOS TV + Wii
releases.body:
Two webOS TV fixes, both found and verified on real hardware.

## Fixed

**The picture was stretched.** The TV compositor always scales the app to fill
the panel and ignores aspect ratio, so the game's 3:2 layout came out
horizontally stretched on a 16:9 screen. The window now carries the panel's
aspect, and the 3:2 playfield is pillarboxed inside it -- black bars at the
sides instead of distorted fruit. Turn WIDESCREEN on in Settings if you would
rather fill the whole screen.

**Menu buttons did not respond.** Slicing worked, but nothing in the menus could
be tapped. LG TVs ship a version of SDL2 that predates the feature the game used
to turn pointer clicks into taps, so presses were silently dropped. The game now
detects that at startup and reads the pointer directly. Buttons, sliders and
scrolling all work with the magic remote.

Wii and desktop builds are unchanged by both fixes.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mariotaku/FruitNinja/compare/v1.6.1-2...v1.6.1-3

releases.name: v1.6.1-2 — webOS TV + Wii
releases.body:
Port release 2 of Fruit Ninja v1.6.1. webOS appinfo version is `1.601.2`.

Input fixes, all in motion mode:

- The motion-mode pointer no longer hijacks menus. Hovering used to register as a held touch, which latched the settings scroller so the list glued itself to the cursor and every widget stopped responding. The blade now has its own touch channel, so clicks stay real press/release for the UI.
- A click no longer cuts. The channel split briefly let a fast button-drag draw a cutting blade.
- No more phantom toggles. Starting a drag on a checkbox and scrolling away left the widget latched, and it resolved that stale touch as a click on its next tick.

Also a README rewrite and the removal of some stale docs.

Unofficial fan project, not affiliated with Halfbrick. These packages bundle the original game data and are not for redistribution.

- **Exact polygon-shape foreground rendering.** Scanline-based fill replaces the previous per-triangle bounding-box scissor, so concave foregrounds like the lower-left obstacle cluster no longer over-cover the actor.
- **Walk-behind Y-sort.** When the actor's feet Y is below a foreground polygon's bottom edge, the polygon no longer draws over the actor. Walk in front of ground obstacles, behind vertical objects like the mooring post.
- **Walkbox tightened around the lower-left crate.** No more walking straight through it.
- **Two new foreground polygons** added for the lamp post and a small upper-left object.

## Running

Unchanged from v0.1.0:
- **macOS:** unzip, double-click `scumm-game.app`. First-launch Gatekeeper: right-click → Open, or allow in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
- **Windows:** unzip, run `scumm-game.exe`. Keep it in the same folder as `assets/`, `sprites/`, etc.

## Controls (reminder)

Play: click verb, click object, click floor to walk. `D` debug overlay.

Edit (`E`): `W` walkbox · `F` cycle fg · `N` new fg · `Backspace` delete fg · `O` auto-order · `R` reset · `S` save. Wheel to zoom, middle-click to pan, `Z` to reset view.

Sprite browser (`B`): arrows to navigate · `0` idle · `1-4` walk · `5-8` face · `S` save.

releases.name: v0.1.0 — First playable release
releases.body:
First release of scumm-game, a SCUMM-style point-and-click adventure engine in C + raylib.

One room (the Monkey Island dock), Guybrush as the actor, plus the editor tooling to shape walkboxes and foregrounds.

## What's in this release

- **Engine:** Dijkstra pathfinding over walkbox vertex visibility, ear-clipped foreground polygons with bg re-sampling, perspective-scaled animated actor sprites, verb bar (Look / Use / Pick up).
- **Walkbox + foreground editor** (`E`): add / drag / delete vertices, cycle between foregrounds, auto-order by centroid, warn on self-intersection. Mouse-wheel **zoom** (anchored at cursor) and middle-click pan for precise vertex placement.
- **Sprite browser** (`B`): pick frames and assign them to animation slots.
- Walkbox and foreground data saved to plain-text `walkbox.txt` / `fg.txt`.

## Running

- **macOS:** unzip, double-click `scumm-game.app`. The app is unsigned, so the first time you may need to right-click → Open, or allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
- **Windows:** unzip, run `scumm-game.exe`. Everything's in the same folder — don't move the .exe out.

## Controls

**Play:** Left-click a verb, then an object, or click the floor to walk. `D` toggles the walkbox/foreground debug overlay.

**Edit mode (`E`):** `W` walkbox · `F` cycle foregrounds · `N` new foreground · `Backspace` delete foreground · `O` auto-order vertices · `R` reset · `S` save. Wheel to zoom, middle-click to pan, `Z` to reset view.

**Sprite browser (`B`):** `←/→` prev/next · `↑/↓` ±10 · `0` idle · `1-4` walk directions · `5-8` face directions · `S` save.

releases.name: v0.1.15 — Wrifthold Rises
releases.body:
The realm has a capital at last. **WRIFTHOLD** — a walled city of twenty-five rooms, every tile and every prop placed by hand.

## THE CITY
Enter by the south gate and the Royal Way runs straight to the castle mouth, crossing the Cross Way at the Grand Plaza and its fountain. Off the ways: twin pond parks, a knot-garden parterre, two market squares trading under a market cross, a packed shop district, orchards in working rows, a dense residential quarter — and a cathedral with a gothic west front whose doors open.

## THE CROWN INN
The capital's great tavern, bespoke inside and out. Drink in the taproom by a live-burning hearth, climb the stairs to a lodging loft of private rooms. Its chimney smokes all day.

## THE GUILDHALL COMES HOME
The one hall in the realm now stands on Wrifthold's forecourt green, its restoration campaign shared across every city board.

## CITY LIFE
Citizens walk the full length of the streets, facing where they're going. Koi rise in the park ponds — a catch found nowhere else — and mallards paddle and dawdle on the water.

## LIGHT AND SHADOW
Street lamps burn at dusk and actually cast their light. Every light in the game now falls off softly instead of ending in a hard ring, and buildings — town fronts, roadside shops, the guildhall — throw real shadows.

## ALSO IN THIS BUILD
- Tree canopies no longer vanish at a room's edge when you cross the seam
- The codex map draws the capital as a city: roads, kerbs, walls, water
- Gate approaches carry causeways over water and cut through rock
- Market stalls keep their own ledgers; six per square
- Lilypads are visible again (missing since the swamp went in)

releases.name: v0.1.14 — Crown & Cobble
releases.body:
## THE CASTLE TOWN
A WALLED CAPITAL now stands in every world — one city, found on the zone-3 ring, built room by room: a living castle in the north wall, the Royal Way running gate to plaza to keep, and a grand fountain plaza where the ways cross.

## THE CITY
- OPEN-AIR MARKETS east and west of the plaza — six themed stalls with vendors at the counters
- A SHOP DISTRICT with every trade you know from the towns — blacksmith, fletcher, magic shop, alchemist, jeweler and more — packed on a sidewalk-trimmed high street
- A RESIDENTIAL DISTRICT of varied homes, orchards with apple-hung trees, pond gardens with lilypads, parterre gardens, a statue garden and commons green
- THE CATHEDRAL QUARTER: rose window, lamplit courtyard, and a hedge-walled graveyard

## A LIVING CITY
CITIZENS ROAM THE WHOLE CAPITAL — walking the roads from gate to castle door, turning at the plaza, pausing to face you. Follow someone out of a room and find them further down the way.

## THE LOOK
- Brick-red cobbled ways with grey kerb trim, gate to gate
- Bespoke castle stone, clipped hedges, topiary avenues, banner poles, sentinel statues
- Flowerbeds along the ways and wildflowers across every lawn

releases.name: v0.1.13 "The Guilds Return"
releases.body:
## THE GUILDS RETURN
- The guildhall is now a CAMPAIGN. Each wing hangs a set of three named bundles - fifteen in all, every one a distinct hunt: species surveys for the Anglers, the ore ladder for the Smiths, book-making materials for the Scholars, real cooked dishes for the Provisioners, a farming year for the Tillers. Every bundle pays on the spot; the last one brings the guild home.
- CEREMONY: completing a wing fires the full-screen banner, the fanfare, and a crest-colored burst off the altar. Candles light, cobwebs fall, and the wing fills with life.
- THRIVING WINGS: restored wings bustle - named guild members, wall banners, and 23 bespoke props (a glowing forge, trophy fish, floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, the feast table).
- THE GRAND ALTARS: towering crest banners over stone offering daises, candles that light when the order returns.
- ALL FIVE PERKS LIVE: anglers' fish prices, provisioners' free inn, smiths' finer shelves, the tillers' produce stall OPENS in their city, and libraries now SELL TOMES - half price where the Scholars are home.
- CONTRACTS and STANDING: restored wings post daily jobs. Fill them for coin and standing - APPRENTICE to JOURNEYMAN to MASTER - and the specialists' storehouses run deeper with your rank. Master smiths sell voidsteel.
- The steward keeps the entry hall; the great hall wears a crest gallery that lights guild by guild.

## THE TOWN GOSSIPS
- Villagers now trade in RUMORS: folk hearsay that happens to be true. Keepers talk their trade - smiths know ore, taverners know cooking, priests know the old world. Every rumor belongs to one person, forever. Listen around.

## THE CAPITAL RISES (UNDER CONSTRUCTION)
- Somewhere in the third ring of every world, a WALLED CASTLE TOWN now stands: ramparts of dressed castle stone, cobbled streets, a grand south gate with crenellated towers and the kingdom's crest on the arch, and the keep itself built into the north wall - iron-bound doors, lit windows, the Royal Standard flying.
- It is early days: the walls, gates, streets, and castle face are in; the market, the guild seat, and much more arrive in coming patches.

## GONE FISHING, REFINED
- Pool ripples are bold now - and clipped to the water, no more washing onto shore.
- Bites come slower everywhere. Fishing breathes: shore ~2-7s, docks quicker, pools quickest.

## FIXES
- Critters came back: a room first seen at night no longer stays empty of birds and rabbits all day.
- Wild NPC speech no longer garbles into runes (E is E again, even mid-wander).
- The guildhall's bundle book plays fair with controllers - D-pad navigates, A confirms, B backs out - and no menu can open over it.

## FOR THE TINKERERS
- The dev panel SPAWN tab lists the whole bestiary; KITS gained the satchel set and a bundle kit per guild.

releases.name: v0.1.12 "Cast & Crew"
releases.body:
## THE STUDIO CARD
- WriftHeart now opens on the New City Entertainment card: the mark fades in from black at full resolution, the sting hits as it lands, and the title screen surfaces from underneath. Any key skips it.

## GONE FISHING
- FISHING POOLS: rippling schools surface at a random spot in the water each day. Cast onto the ripples for near-instant bites and a better roll on what's hooked - pull three fish and the school moves on to a new spot. Tomorrow they run somewhere else entirely.
- CHARGED CAST: tap the rod for the short flick, hold to wind up and send the bobber up to four tiles out. The line arcs right over rocks and shore - but overshoot onto dry ground and the cast fizzles. Judge your distance.
- DOCKS: some big waters now grow plank piers. Fish from the boards and the fish gather faster under your feet. Some pools sit far enough out that only a dock or a full wind-up reaches them.

## THE WORLD
- Roads no longer pave insane causeways across entire lakes. Long crossings break at the shore; short planks still span brooks.
- Lava no longer flows through towns (or the castle). A molten main street was quite a zoning decision.

## FIXES
- Fixed a crash when an emberling lit its fuse - the walking bomb was missing its HOT frame. It now swells bright orange right before the bang, as intended.
- The dev status strip got a near-opaque backing - legible over bright biomes.

## FOR THE TINKERERS
- The dev panel's SPAWN tab now lists the entire bestiary - every mob as its own row, alphabetized, in a scrolling list. The goblins sort right in with the rest.

releases.name: v0.1.11 — Now You See It
releases.body:
A release about things finally being visible - starting with your armor.

## NOW YOU SEE IT
- WORN ARMOR RENDERS AGAIN: a load-order bug has been painting every hero bare since the save system landed - your helmet, vest, and boots were equipped but invisible. Load a save and you are DRESSED.
- The Miner's Helmet earns its keep: grey steel, and the headlamp reads from all four facings - bold on the brow, a lamp column in profile, the strap and peeking tip from behind.

## THE GOLDEN TOUCH
- GOD MODE wears a breathing GOLD AURA traced around your exact frame - the corner GOD MODE tag is gone; the glow is the tell. Charge a swing while divine and the blue rim stacks over the gold.

## THE MOTHER LODE
- BESPOKE ORE NODES: six hand-drawn rocks - nugget-studded copper, blocky iron, shard-crowned silver, a gold mound, a mithril crystal cluster, a voidsteel monolith. Each pays 2-3 chunks of its metal, a stone, and a 15% GEM.
- Plain boulders are plain now: stone only, any pick opens them. Caves keep their rich stalagmite and crystal-spire veins.

## THE EMBERMAW BEHAVES
- Mobs BURN in lava - ignited with flames, damage, and panic - and everything paths around it... except the FIRE KIN (cinderhound, charbrute, emberling, ashgeyser, pyrewraith), who cross their home turf freely.
- Lava finally shows on the world map and minimap - along with 15 other newer grounds (salt flats white, tar pits black, the void violet) that all baked grey before.
- The stray red corner wedges at lava edges are gone.

## STEADIER HANDS
- The four ability slots are CLICKABLE - click a cell to fire it, no accidental sword swings.
- Q in your bag USES the item instead of flipping tabs (tabs still walk everywhere else).
- The widget arranger reads true: CHARACTER (was VITALS), ITEMS, BUFFS/DEBUFFS, the PINNED BOTTOM section lists top-to-bottom exactly as it renders, margins even all round.
- The Bubble Ring's sphere is smooth, centred on your body at every facing, and no longer floats away during room transitions (nor does the shield flash, the charge aura, or the god glow).
- 29 item icons sit properly centred in their cells - the flute and bubble ring included.

## UNDER THE HOOD
- A rare crash during room transitions can no longer take the game down - stray effects log a warning and play continues.

releases.name: v0.1.10 — Moving Day
releases.body:
Rearrange your sidebar, and watch the whole world ride along.

YOUR SIDEBAR, YOUR WAY
- Every sidebar section is a WIDGET now: vitals, abilities, clock, quests, buffs, a NEW shard tally and coin purse, hints. The ESC menu grew a WIDGETS tab - grab a widget, carry it, pin it TOP or BOTTOM, hide it. Your layout saves with your game.
- Some widgets hide behind ITEMS: no pocket watch, no CLOCK in the menu at all. Find the item and the widget appears.

THE COMPASS KEEPS ITS PROMISE
- Equip the Compass and a LIVE MINIMAP joins the sidebar: real thumbnails of the rooms around you - water, paths, forests - with gold town pips, red dungeon pips, your home in green, and your dot moving tile by tile.

NOTHING POPS ANYMORE
- The whole cast RIDES room transitions now: mobs, villagers, wagons, the guildhall - they slide out with their room and slide in with the next, both directions.
- Torchlight rides too: leave a town at night and the glow leaves WITH the torches instead of cutting out.

CLAIMING A SHARD IS AN EVENT
- The SHARD RITE: the world goes dark, the shard rises on a pillar of light, the heartbeat pounds, and the land's name burns across the screen.

THE SKY LEARNED DEPTH
- Blizzards rebuilt on four parallax depths: the far snow barely hears the wind while the near flakes race and streak sideways, over a rolling ground-whiteout. No more marching bands of snow.

BALANCE
- Passive tree HP rescaled to the heart economy - no more grinding into an unkillable tank (a dedicated tank build is tough, not immortal).
- REGEN is endgame now: never in the tree, ultra rare, epic+ gear only.
- Skill tree forks are CHOICES: pick a lane, the other seals until you refund.
- The tree got the map's parallax star-void, mouse drag, and honest fork lines.
- The dying knight rolls real rarity dice. Beasts finally carry their hides - boar, wolf, and bear drop leather.
- The SANDMAW: no shadow (it IS a hole), truly immune to knockback, and a TONGUE that snaps out and reels you into the teeth.

ODDS AND ENDS
- The pickaxe head points the right way now (it was upside down, lol).
- Cut giant flowers leave THEIR stalk behind, not someone else's stump.
- Gravestones: four carved variants, no more accidental faces. Pillars: three real broken-column variants.
- Tents you could actually sleep in, war banners worth rallying to - encounter props at human scale.
- Spider nests and spider lairs are WEBBED - cut the webs for string, like the dungeons.
- Town chat garble fixed for good; wild trader prompts speak controller; a full bag auto-equips gear into empty slots; the map's RECENTER chip retired (the hotkey stays).

releases.name: v0.1.9 — Hot Off the Press
releases.body:
The floor is lava, and the library grew.

THE FLOOR IS LAVA
- The Embermaw finally burns: real molten lava with a drifting crust, bursting bubbles, and a glow you can read by.
- Step in and you will know it - a BURNING debuff and damage that ticks until you get out.
- Lava keeps to its homeland: it flows freely through the Embermaw but holds back from foreign borders, so biome edges no longer look cut off.

HOT OFF THE PRESS (18 new books -> 125)
- THE VIGIL ROLL: the last knights of a dead kingdom - their vow, their thirty-year patrols, and the letter every one of them carries for whoever kneels beside them.
- WELLS AND FALLING STARS: what the College will not repeat about well nine, and the smith whose lantern burned dimmer near the metal that fell.
- THE QUIET MAN: five books that circle someone who is always already in the room. Read them in any order. Latch your door.
- THE KINGDOM: the shepherd who found the Hearthstone, a queen and her bees, an unfinished lullaby, and a scavenger who knew the Black Castle floor plan far too well.

A WORLD THAT TALKS
- Town chatter now follows the story: as shards are gathered, the talk of the day changes - news, rumors, hope, and worse.

POLISH
- Cultists are PEOPLE now: hooded, robed figures in the field and the bestiary, not blobs.
- The Witherheart's drain orbs got real art (no more yellow squares).
- The loot goblin respects walls. Tents fit their sleepers. The dying knight speaks clearly.
- Dev panel shows both tier ladders, and crater ore now matches the threat of the ground it fell on.

releases.name: v0.1.8 — Who Goes There
releases.body:
You will never know what the next room holds.

THE WORLD MOVES ON
- Beaten camps no longer stay gone forever: cleared ground lies quiet for half a season, then something NEW may move in - or the wilderness simply returns. The world keeps living behind you.
- The wilds now run on clocks: some things only happen at NIGHT, some only in a season, and some roam to a different room every single day.

WHO GOES THERE (25 encounters -> 107)
- Hordes: face THE HUNGRY DEAD (22 zombies under the moon), THE MARCHING LEGION, THE WARHOST, THE SLIME FLOOD, and more.
- Firelight: five travelers telling TALES BY FIRELIGHT, a COUNTRY WEDDING, pilgrims, foragers, stargazers, mourners.
- Dread: a camp that is TOO QUIET, THE ABANDONED RITE, THE LARDER, an invisible something you should not follow.
- Fortune: a DYING KNIGHT offers his blade with his last breath. A fallen star waits in THE CRATER, heavy with rare ore. A merchant with four possible faces. An ancient WELL that whispers - toss it a coin. Sometimes it knows your name.
- Gambles: beasts asleep on piles of gold. Take it quietly... or take one step too close.
- THE ALPHA now leads the wolves. The SANDMAW is as big as it always should have been.

COMBAT
- A blocked arrow now RICOCHETS off your shield, just like the old days.
- The sword's spin attack is a real whirl you can see - and your hero turns with the blade.

POLISH
- Talk prompts near every villager and wanderer; overhead text no longer garbles.
- Fewer quest-givers crowding every town; towns announce once, at their gates.
- Click any cell in the bestiary, items, and lore collections.
- HP/MP values centered, MP shows numbers, a dozen small alignment fixes.

releases.name: v0.1.7 — Ask For Directions
releases.body:
The world finally tells you where to go.

NEW
- THE FIRST QUEST LINE: a lone survivor waits in the ashes of Emberfall. Talk to her, take THE LAST EMBER, and follow it to your first axe, pick, and shard.
- DODGE-STEP: quick invincible dash on SPACE / right trigger. With your shield up, the same button is a SHIELD BASH that staggers foes.
- HOLD MOVES: hold the button to charge each weapon's own special — the sword SPIN, the axe CLEAVE, the pick SHATTER. Watch for the blue glow.
- Your shield now blocks melee hits from the front, not just arrows.
- TALK prompt when you're near villagers.
- MAP GLOW-UP: quest arrows on the map's edge point toward your objectives, unexplored quest targets get a marked tile, the grid runs edge to edge, and the whole fold floats on a drifting starlit void.
- Banners wear sharp shadows; the death screen names what killed you; where you fell is marked on the map for the day.

FIXED
- The map pan dead zone (that one-second delay before it moved).
- Panning accelerates the longer you hold.
- First day always dawns clear; critters no longer panic in corners; plus a pile of smaller fixes.

releases.name: v0.1.6 — Skill Issue
releases.body:
The passive tree grew up, the sky grew teeth, and your killer signs their work.

**THE SKILL TREE, RETHOUGHT**
- Every node is now its own reward — no more rows of identical +2% dots. Bigger numbers, real choices
- New powers in the constellation: knockback, attack speed, mercy frames, armor
- Stats that were quietly doing nothing now WORK: spell damage, max MP, and mana regen from the tree reach your wand and flute; attack speed speeds attacks; mercy frames widen your hurt window
- Your allocated points carry over — same tree shape, new rewards

**A NEW LOOK**
- The word-art WRIFTHEART logo crowns the title screen and the story crawl
- The loot goblin finally wears his stuffed backpack — and glints gold in the dark as he flees
- Giant flowers leave a proper cut stem behind, not a woodcutter's stump

**THE WORLD BITES BACK**
- Thunderstorm lightning now strikes for real: trees, bushes and grass catch fire (the storm's own rain can't douse a lightning-born burn), and anything standing under the bolt gets hurt
- Water spitters relocate with every dive — no more camping one ripple
- The death screen names your killer, and a gravestone on the map marks where you fell — walk back the same day to reclaim your scattered bag

**BUILD AND UNBUILD**
- Hold the trash key beside your house, coop, barn, or well to pack it up for half its cost — craft tables still tear down from their own menu
- Fresh heroes start with just a sword and shield, the classic way

**SHOPS AND SCREENS**
- The shop is a two-pane window: browse on the left, examine on the right — icon, rarity, price, and lore
- Controller play hides the mouse; touching the mouse brings it back
- ESC backs out of title menus, naming your hero starts from a blank box, and quest marks sit centered in their plates

**FIXES**
- New games no longer inherit a previous save's house, stash, or respawn (dying no longer teleports you to a home you never built)
- Books and placed stones ride room transitions instead of popping
- Critters remember where they wandered when you step out and back
- Weather cuts off indoors and greets you at full strength when you step back out — and every adventure begins on a clear day

releases.name: v0.1.5 — Making Waves
releases.body:
The lakes came alive.

**THE WATER**
- All-new living water: a painted surface that drifts, ripples, glints, and chops up in storms — deep blue lakes, murky green swamps
- Water now flows smoothly through room transitions
- Coastlines curve properly everywhere — no more blocky corners or that pasted-on blue border
- Hedges hang their leafy edges out over the waterline

**NEW DANGERS IN THE DEEP**
- Rare water lurkers now haunt lakes and swamps: spitters that surface and fire, tentacles that lash from the shallows — with poison and chilling variants by biome
- Enemy shots (and yours) now sail over water — nothing hides behind a river anymore

**THE WORLD**
- Trees shake loose drifting leaves when struck — blossom trees shed pink petals
- The miner's helmet casts a true cone of light
- Trees drop their biome's own timber: petalwood, gloomwood, charwood, mirewood, frostpine
- Critters flee corners cleverly instead of panicking — truly cornered, they cower

**FIXES & POLISH**
- Venom rune: poison spray + lingering puddles
- Buffs and quest tracker no longer overlap; the mouse wheel scrolls menus
- Weather cuts off instantly indoors
- The loot goblin can no longer run on water
- Dev panel: clickable rows, more kits, honest WARP HOME

releases.name: v0.1.4 — Toxic Trait
releases.body:
The wand learns its wickedest trick yet — and the dungeons got a deep-clean.

## ☠️ The Venom Rune
- A **fourth rune** joins the wand: craft it at the Enchanter's Table (find the blueprint, or check the magic shops)
- **VENOM SPRAY**: a fan of purple droplets that **poisons** whatever it splashes — poisoned foes turn purple, bubble ominously, and sicken over time
- Every third droplet leaves a **poison puddle** on the ground; enemies standing in one stay envenomed as long as they linger. Herd them through it.

## 🏰 Dungeon Polish
- Wall torches **flicker** now instead of standing frozen
- Dungeon keys show at the **bottom-left**, out of the notification feed's way
- The ornate-key chest stands **alone** — no more mystery twin beside it (the treasure chest appears after you've claimed the key)
- The end-of-dungeon **warp rune** is reborn from the classic version: a living pulse of violet light with orbiting motes — it sits **grey and dormant until you claim the shard**, then wakes and offers **ACTIVATE** on a press. No more accidental exits.

## 🧑‍🌾 Farm Where You Live
- The hoe now tills **any clear ground** — sand, snow, ash, all of it. Your homestead's biome no longer decides whether you get to farm.
- When the hoe refuses, it now **tells you why** (town ground, something in the way, a growing crop)

## 🎒 Odds & Ends
- **M always opens the MAP** — no more reopening whatever codex page you last browsed
- **Satchels work**: use one from your bag and the next row of inventory unlocks on the spot
- Frozen enemies wear a **deeper blue**; the AWARDS page header no longer hides under the tabs
- Fixed a crash that could kill the game the instant it launched

releases.name: v0.1.3 — Cold Snap
releases.body:
The frost wand found its true form — and half the game's menus got manners.

## ❄️ The Frost Beam
- The frost rune now fires an instant **beam of ice** instead of a bolt — thick, bright, and cold
- It sails **over water**, stops at bushes, trees, and rocks, and bites the first foe it touches
- Frozen enemies are **frozen solid for 5 seconds**: ice-blue, wreathed in frost mist, statue-still, and safe to walk past — works on beasts and goblinkind alike

## 🔥 Real Fire
- Enemies hit by firebolts now **catch fire properly** — clinging flames, burning damage, and beasts **run around in a blind panic** while they burn
- Fire's look matches the classic version: glowing tongues and the white-hot spark
- A blaze now slides out with its room instead of hanging in the air

## 🎵 Song of Returning
- **HOME leads the warp list** when you have a house — and lands you on your doorstep
- The full warp ceremony is back: the channel with counter-rotating rings, climbing sparks, swelling light, and the hero **spinning down into the portal** — take a hit mid-song and it breaks

## 🛠️ Benches & Building
- Crafting stations open **their own menu**, separate from your pack — and the Enchanter's Table gains a **RUNES tab** to imbue your wand at the source
- Station kits and the house **place straight from the bag** — no equipping first
- Tables can now be placed **inside your house**

## ⚙️ Odds & Ends
- Recipe pinning, crafting from the home chest, and blueprints usable from the bag
- Glimmerling beams finally aim true (every beam in the game drew crooked — now fixed)
- The guildhall donation menu no longer plays your flute when you try to close it
- Shop prices unmangled, armor stats signed properly, elite name tags un-garbled
- God mode (dev): free crafting, bottomless coin purse, endless mana — your real money returns the moment it's off

releases.name: v0.1.2 — Home Improvement
releases.body:
**This one's about making your house a home.** 🏡

## New
- **Ghost placement** — placing a workbench, forge, or your House now shows a movable preview: green means it fits, red means it won't. Rotate tables with Ability 3, cancel free.
- **Crafting benches got a furniture upgrade** — proper table bodies with four facings and per-craft dressings; the forge is a real stone furnace now.
- **Remove a bench** from its craft window and get half the materials back.
- **A brand-new farmhouse** — your built home finally looks like one: gabled roof, chimney, shuttered windows, flowerboxes, a lantern by the door.
- **Home sweet home** — your home room is a safe zone (no monster spawns), benches there craft straight from your storage chest, and the hearth fire actually burns.
- **Set your spawn** — choose REST or SET SPAWN at your bed; inns offer REST AND SET SPAWN. Fall in battle and wake where you chose.
- **Dungeon keys live on your screen now** (bottom-right), not in your bag — and they stay behind when you leave.
- **Boots straight to the title** — the audio engine warms up in the background instead of freezing the launch.

## Fixed
- Four enemies that attacked while *invisible* now have bodies (the Prismwastes crystal among them). Fair fights only.
- The glimmerling's light-beam aims where you actually are — and no longer flings you across the room.
- The same tree/boulder is now cuttable everywhere in its biome (no more "needs a stronger axe" one room over).
- Sound effects for chopping, mining, hitting, getting hit, enemy defeats, coins, and pickups — the world makes noise again.
- Songs cast when you *release* the final note, so the phrase resolves naturally.
- Map: panning is smooth and controllable, town names render crisply, mystery squares removed.
- Cobwebs drop string; dungeon crystals are genuinely minable (bring a pick — they drop gems).
- Shadows read better; the inventory panel visibly slides; a bench no longer swallows your head mid-swing.

The first native release of WriftHeart — the Rust + Bevy rewrite.

Recover the ten shards, mend the WriftHeart, and face what waits in the Black Castle.

releases.name: v0.57.0 — Speed HUD, Distinct Colors, Mechanic Sharing
releases.body:
## What's New

- **In-game speed control**: 1x / 2x / 4x buttons visible during bot simulation
- **Distinct bot colors**: 9 colors pushed further apart for maximum visual clarity
- **Mechanic tile sharing**: bots can cross each other's Turn/Arrow tiles
- **Project cleanup**: simplified to single `protocol-play-player` binary
- **All 149 campaign levels** regenerated with improved generator

## Download

Extract and run:
```sh
tar xzf protocol-play-player-linux.tar.gz
cd protocol-play-player-linux
./protocol-play-player
```

## What's New

### Cumulative mechanics across chapters
Each chapter introduces ONE new mechanic, then ALL subsequent levels mix it with everything learned before. By Chapter 10, levels use 11+ mechanic types simultaneously.

### Proper difficulty curve
- **Intro level**: only the new mechanic (learn it)
- **Levels 2-4**: new mechanic dominant, previous ones light
- **Levels 5-8**: balanced mix of all mechanics
- **Boss levels 9-11**: everything cranked up equally

### Level composition
| Chapter | Bots | Board | Inventory | Board mechs | Types |
|---------|------|-------|-----------|-------------|-------|
| 1 | 1→4 | 3→8 | 1→12 | 0→12 | 1 |
| 5 | 3→7 | 5→10 | 3→16 | 0→40+ | 3-5 |
| 10 | 3→8 | 5→11 | 6→18 | 0→48 | 6-11 |
| 13 | 5→10 | 8→12 | 10→18 | 0→79 | 3-13 |
| Finals | 10 | 12 | 15-18 | 59-79 | 12-13 |

### Algorithm
- Up to 10 bots with smart placement and auto path-sharing
- Dense mechanic boards (50-80% of cells)
- Varied holes (edges/middle/both, rotating pattern)

## Bevy 0.18 Migration

Upgraded the entire codebase from Bevy 0.15 to Bevy 0.18, covering all 22 source files across both the Bot Game and The Gathering modules.

### Key API changes applied:
- `single()`/`single_mut()` now returns `Result` — all system functions updated
- `BorderColor` changed from tuple to named-field struct
- `BorderRadius` moved from standalone component into `Node` struct
- `ChildBuilder` → `ChildSpawnerCommands`
- `AmbientLight` → `GlobalAmbientLight`
- `Bloom` moved to `bevy::post_process::bloom`
- `despawn_recursive()` → `despawn()`
- `Parent` → `ChildOf`
- HDR now default on `Camera3d`

### No gameplay changes
All existing features remain identical — this is a pure engine upgrade.

## What's New

### Colored Teleports
- **Teleport tiles** now support 11 colors (10 + grey for all bots)
  - Grey teleports affect **all** bots (same as before)
  - Colored teleports affect **only matching color** bots — others pass through
- **TeleportBut tiles** — new tile type: teleports all bots **except** matching color
  - Ring + 7-segment number + forbidden symbol visual
  - 10 color variants

### Auto-Numbering
- Numbers are **automatically assigned** — no manual number selection in inventory
- Each (type, color) combination has independent numbering (up to 10 pairs)
- Unpaired numbers get completed first, then unused numbers are allocated
- Ghost preview shows the correct auto-assigned number while hovering

### Technical
- Removed `PlacedTeleports` resource — auto-numbering computed from board tiles
- 210 new colored materials (110 Teleport + 100 TeleportBut)
- New `teleportbut` procedural textures (ring + number + forbidden symbol)
- `next_teleport_number()` helper for consistent auto-numbering across ghost and placement

releases.body:
## Changes since v0.13.0

### Ghost & Hover Improvements
- **Ghost fade-out trails**: hovering between tiles now leaves smooth fade-out trails instead of abrupt jumps
- **Exact-match ghost suppression**: no ghost animation when hovering over a tile identical to what would be placed (same type + direction + color)
- **Dialog dismiss ghost suppression**: after closing any modal dialog, ghost is suppressed until mouse moves to a different tile

### Player/Editor Consistency
- Player inventory slots now match editor sizing (slot_node)
- Player count text format matches editor ("2" not "x2")
- Player count text positioned at bottom like editor L3 slots
- Player eraser button matches editor (transparent background, no border)

### UI Polish
- Darker empty tile grid markers for better visibility
- Eraser button same size as other L1 inventory slots
- Count text color changed to dark grey
- Editor inventory fully hidden during test mode (-500px)
- L2/L3 slots animate in with width grow + opacity fade

### Code Quality
- Extracted `suppress_ghost()` helper to reduce repeated pattern
- `dp!()`/`place!()` macros for cleaner tile placement code

releases.name: v0.13.0 - Colored Switches, Crush, & PNG Pipeline
releases.body:
## New Features
- **Colored switches**: `ColorSwitch` tiles only toggle doors for matching-color bots; `ColorSwitchBut` tiles toggle for all bots EXCEPT the specified color
- **Bot crush mechanic**: Bots caught by closing doors get crushed with a squash animation (Y→0, XZ expand 1.5x)
- **Alternative solution detection**: Shows "Solved with pieces to spare!" when test mode is completed with unused inventory pieces
- **Non-interactive level tiles in test mode**: Level-designed tiles no longer respond to hover, ghost preview, or clicks during test mode

## Technical Improvements
- **Unified PNG texture pipeline**: All tile types (including teleports) now use base+mask PNG files — edit PNGs in `assets/textures/` to customize both 3D tiles and inventory icons
- **textures.rs reduced** from 387 to 239 lines by removing duplicated shape functions
- **Cleaner gen_textures.rs**: Existence check uses loop instead of 30-line boolean chain

- `protocol-play-player` — Player mode (Linux x86_64)

releases.name: v0.10.0 - Bot clusters and unlimited sources/goals
releases.body:
## What's new in v0.10.0

### Bot cluster rendering
Bots no longer z-fight when they share a tile. Each bot gets a unique fixed world-space XZ offset based on its spawn order, so overlapping bots naturally form a small visible cluster — whether they converge on the same tile, travel together, or cross paths.

### Multiple sources/goals per color
The 1-source-per-color and 1-goal-per-color restrictions have been removed. You can now place as many sources or goals of the same color as your puzzle requires. This also removes the confusing auto-advance behavior on placement.

### Technical
- `BOT_XZ_OFFSETS` constant: 10 fixed offsets in a grid/cross pattern
- `spawn_index` field on `BotMovement` tracks each bot's unique offset
- Removed `PlacedSources` and `PlacedGoals` resources and all associated tracking/gate logic

releases.name: v0.9.0 - Arrow and ArrowBut tiles
releases.body:
## What's new

### Arrow tile
Forces every bot to follow the arrow's direction — including 180° U-turns when the arrow points opposite to the bot's travel. Grey variant affects all bots; 10 colored variants affect bots of that color.

### ArrowBut tile (Color Arrow)
Same redirecting behavior for non-matching bots. Bots of the tile's color cannot follow the arrow and are bounced back instead. 10 colors.

### Bug fix
BounceColor and BounceButColor slots were silently skipped in the inventory expansion (rebuild_l3_colors). Both now appear correctly.

## Technical
- Two new TileKind variants: `Arrow(usize, Direction)`, `ArrowBut(usize, Direction)`
- Full simulation logic: arrow redirect and ArrowBut per-color bounce
- Isometric icons with rotation variants for all 4 directions
- File-based tile textures auto-generated on first run (arrow_base.png, arrow_mask.png, etc.)
- All source files remain ≤400 lines

releases.name: v0.5.0 - File-based textures & color memory
releases.body:
## What's New

### Two-texture emission system
- Base texture defines shape and stroke (dark gray)
- Color mask controls where and how strongly the programmatic color is applied via emissive
- Turn center circle now correctly shows a dark version of the tile's color

### Editable file-based textures
- Symbol textures auto-generated as PNGs in `assets/textures/` on first run
- Edit the PNGs to customize tile appearance — changes apply everywhere
- Base textures: `source_base.png`, `turn_base.png` (shape + stroke)
- Color masks: `source_mask.png`, `turn_mask.png` (emission intensity)

### Color memory
- Switching between Source and Turn tools remembers the last placed color
- No more defaulting to orange after placing a red source and switching to Turn

### Other improvements
- Turn L3 color slots show ∞ amount indicator
- Textures loaded synchronously for reliable rendering
- Mask textures loaded as linear for correct color multiplication

releases.name: v0.4.0 — Turn tiles & modular codebase
releases.body:
## What's New

### Turn Tiles
- New **Turn tile** type with L-shaped corner piece symbol
- Dark-colored center circle matching the tile's color
- 10 distinct colors, same as Source tiles
- Unlimited placement per color (shown as ∞ in inventory)
- Full inventory integration: L1 → L2 direction → L3 color selection

### Modular Codebase
- Split monolithic `main.rs` (2042 lines) into 7 clean modules (all ≤400 lines):
  - `constants.rs` — all named constants for colors, sizes, speeds
  - `types.rs` — enums, resources, components
  - `textures.rs` — procedural texture and icon generation
  - `board.rs` — tile spawning, board controls, play/stop, camera
  - `inventory.rs` — slot helpers, interaction, visuals
  - `systems.rs` — animations, hover, ghost/highlight, tile placement
  - `main.rs` — app setup and UI construction

### Constants-Driven Styling
- All colors, sizes, animation speeds, and geometry values extracted into named constants
- Easy to tweak visual appearance from a single file
